timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only Claude CLI stream for the serial run; no projected semantic events.
Serial parent trajectory: black-box probing, implementation, local Rust differential harness, cargo/rustc verification, final response, and normal closure.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the black-box C++ entry point, exact seven-line output contract, Rust 2021/std-only requirement, Cargo project layout, and root test7.rs deliverable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation and local tests, then delegated differential verification to a workflow with ten broad child lenses and retry handling.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a modular URL parser, initially string-oriented, then after child invalid-UTF8 findings began byte-oriented helper rewrites; official artifact passed 40/40.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Created Cargo.toml, library modules, root test7.rs, and executable artifacts; artifact validation succeeded even though final response was empty after timeout.
parallel.verification: Ran manual probes, 100-case corpus, cargo tests, exhaustive ASCII sweeps, and a broad child verifier workflow, but the workflow never returned aggregate audit/critic results.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Process timed out with return code 143 and no final response; verifier retry/audit lifecycle remained incomplete, but official evaluator passed the artifact.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same black-box interface, exact CLI/output behavior, Rust 2021/std-only project, root entry file, and Cargo deliverables.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single actor retained ownership of probing, implementation, module organization, differential harness, tests, rebuild, and final response.
serial.implementation: Implemented a compact parser.rs plus numeric helper that captured scheme/order, authority reconstruction, stoi-like ports, host-based validity, and ASCII lowercasing.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Created the Cargo project, root test7.rs, library files, and executable, then listed deliverables and gave a final migration summary.
serial.verification: Ran a Rust differential harness for 32,473 cases, checked documented examples, ran cargo test, rebuilt, and re-ran the differential check before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished trajectory issue is visible; serial completed normally and official evaluator passed 40/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized pure Rust 2021, Cargo project, root test7.rs, black-box inference, exact CLI and byte-for-byte output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same black-box task requirements and no-dependency Rust/Cargo deliverables.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement recognition gap; both solved the same interface and official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent owned implementation and launched a verifier workflow with ten child lenses for differential testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Single actor owned probing, implementation, verification, cleanup, and final response without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel separated verification into many child attempts; serial kept ownership local and finished cleanly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Verifier children received a shared binary/source context and scratch-file guidance, but stalled retries restarted from generic context rather than inherited checkpoints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No inter-actor context transfer was needed; the same actor retained discovered parser rules through implementation and testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel retry context was lossy for verifier progress, while serial maintained continuity in one trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Built a modular Rust port, discovered a high-byte argv issue from verifier scratch, and began converting helpers to byte-oriented parsing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Built a compact parser module and numeric helper after probing stoi, authority reconstruction, and is_valid host semantics.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached passing artifacts by black-box inference, but parallel incorporated child-discovered byte handling under timeout pressure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow result never returned; the workflow state is killed and the parent process timed out despite an evaluator-passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed its local verification loop, listed deliverables, and sent a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left verifier lifecycle and final response unfinished; serial completed lifecycle and closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent and child verifiers used shared /output and /workspace/scratch state; some verifier logs mention concurrent source updates and output interleaving.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one local workspace and did not coordinate with child-owned scratch or verifier state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had noisier shared-state management, but no proven final artifact corruption; serial had simpler provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local probes/tests, launched broad child differential testing, consumed a child invalid-UTF8 finding, but the workflow audit/critic and aggregate acceptance did not complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a Rust differential harness, ran 32,473 cases with zero mismatches, ran cargo test, rebuilt, and re-ran the differential check.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had complete self-contained acceptance evidence; parallel had much broader attempted verification but unfinished aggregate verifier lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full agent budget, returned code 143 for agent_timeout, and final.txt is empty, while the evaluator still passed the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 654 seconds, returned code 0, had substantial remaining budget, and produced a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was forced by budget exhaustion; serial closure was normal.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official completed evaluations show both parallel and serial solutions passed 40/40, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete difference is process lifecycle: serial completed a local implementation and verification loop with a final response, while parallel created an official-passing artifact but exhausted budget inside a retried verifier workflow and ended without a workflow return or final message.
parallel_contributors: Parent implementation and child-discovered invalid-UTF8 issue contributed to an evaluator-passing artifact.
Checkpoint-free verifier retries contributed to timeout and incomplete closure rather than to an official failure.
serial_contributors: Serial kept context and verification local, ran 32,473 differential cases, cargo tests, and final rebuild checks.
Serial completed with return code 0 and a final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial used a compact parser.rs/numeric.rs design; parallel used more modules and a late byte-oriented rewrite path.
Both implementations were sufficient for the official evaluator, so these are strategy differences rather than failure causes.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator scores the artifact and passed the parallel solution despite process timeout and empty final.txt.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern explains adverse parallel process closure only

candidates.reason: The parallel parent actively owned and wrote the Rust implementation before launching verifier children.
There were no separately owned implementation components needing an unassigned reconciler; the parent owned integration.
The parent created the Cargo project, entry file, and executable artifact, so final assembly was assigned.
The parent owned probing, implementation, local tests, workflow launch, and artifact delivery; the issue was retry handling, not missing pipeline ownership.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent implemented before the workflow.
Parallel did not defer all productive implementation until investigation children returned; implementation preceded child verification.
The adverse episode is not auxiliary work starving an unstaffed implementation path; it is checkpoint-free verifier retry consumption.
Broad fan-out and many children are visible, but the retained direct boundary is uncheckpointed stalled retries sharing the same timeout consequence.
Individual verifier lenses were broad, but no single child scope is the distinct retained cause apart from the retry loop.
Verifier briefs stated the task, binaries, no-output-write rule, scratch guidance, and reporting schema; no known requirement omission produced unusable work.
Children were verifiers rather than separately owned implementation components, and the scratch naming rule provided the relevant interface guidance.
No known finding disappeared through a transfer; the parent observed the key invalid-UTF8 child finding through scratch output.
The workflow did not return a large completed handoff that the parent failed to reduce; it was killed before aggregate return.
Children observed live workspace changes, but no transferred handoff was consumed after becoming superseded.
No incompatible completed reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision in the parallel final; official pass came from evaluator artifacts after timeout.
Stalled workflow verifier lenses were retried with the same generic prompt and no visible carried-forward checkpoint, causing repeated setup/probing and unfinished verifier return before timeout.
candidates.realized_consequence: Repeated verifier retry attempts consumed the parallel run budget and left workflow return, audit/critic phases, and final response incomplete.
candidates.near_match_reason: Fan-out is visible, but for this episode the directly correctable boundary is the checkpoint-free retry of stalled verifier work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Child interruptions are downstream of the same killed workflow/retry chain rather than a separate explicit cancellation boundary.
The required artifact was already present and passed official evaluation; the missing final message is not unplaced deliverable packaging.
Late byte-oriented edits occurred under the same unfinished verifier retry chain; no separate post-merge lifecycle consequence is isolated from that retained episode.
No completed delegated implementation was left unjoined; child agents were verifiers, not implementation owners.
The absent aggregate verifier return is the terminal symptom of the retained checkpoint-free retry chain, not a separate result-lifecycle episode.
The parent consumed an important child finding and began work; unfinished stalled verifier children belong to the same retained retry chain.
The parent inspected available scratch results and used the invalid-UTF8 finding; no visible completed child result was ignored.
The parent repeatedly checked workflow/scratch progress and did not simply wait blindly to the deadline.
No competing child-owned implementation files with overlapping behavior were produced for reconciliation.
No two live implementation agents are proven to edit the same source file and reconcile each other's changes.
The parent rewrote its own sources; there is no proven replacement of another agent's non-entry source file.
A local background rebuild caused transient test noise, but no other agent-owned deliverable was proven overwritten as a retained coordination episode.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced multiple final outputs and invalidated another agent's final tree work.
Shared scratch/output visibility caused noise but not a proven multi-agent implementation-write provenance failure beyond the retained retry episode.
No generated artifact from one child is shown to have been consumed by another as authoritative stable input and to contaminate final behavior.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel workflow repeatedly retried stalled verifier lenses without handing the replacement a checkpoint or next deliverable milestone; replacement children re-read harness/source context and repeated setup work, and the workflow was killed before it returned.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Verifier retry churn consumed the remaining parallel budget, leaving the workflow aggregate, audit/critic phases, and final response incomplete even though the artifact later passed official evaluation.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The same timeout chain includes broad fan-out, but retaining fan-out would duplicate the unchanged-retry episode and consequence.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Missing Verifier Return, Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were treated as near or downstream descriptions of the same stalled verifier retry/timeout chain rather than separate labels.
Merge after Verification was rejected because the late edit/no-post-merge-check symptom was not independent of the retained verifier retry budget episode.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the directly evidenced checkpoint-free verifier retry clears the paired retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No additional timeout, child interruption, missing return, fan-out, or shared-state label was retained without distinct anchors, consequence, and corrective action.
